title: My weekend in Uralsk
paragraphs: My name is Aruzhan Bekova. I am nineteen years old and I am from Kyzylorda. I study Engineering at WKU — it is my first year and I love it. Last weekend was one of the best weekends I have had since I moved to Uralsk. I want to tell you about everything I did, because every moment of it was special in some way.

On Saturday morning, I woke up at half past seven — earlier than usual for a weekend! I immediately cleaned my room from top to bottom. I washed the floor, dusted the shelves, and organised my textbooks by subject. It only took forty minutes, but afterwards the room looked beautiful and I felt so much better. Then I cooked a simple breakfast — scrambled eggs with tomatoes and a big cup of green tea. I listened to a Kazakh music playlist while I cooked, and I hummed along to every song.

After breakfast, I called my mother in Kyzylorda. We talked for nearly an hour. She asked about my studies, my food, my friends, and my sleep — the usual things mothers ask! I told her everything and she laughed a lot. My younger brother joined the call and showed me his new football boots. I missed them both so much after that call. But talking to them also energised me and I felt ready for the rest of the day.

In the afternoon, I met my friends outside the WKU gates. There were four of us: me, my classmate Saule, my dormitory friend Aisha, and a boy from the Economics faculty named Yerlan Omarov. We walked to the Uralsk city park — it took about twenty-five minutes on foot. The weather was perfect: cool, sunny, and with a gentle breeze. We walked along the river path, talked about our lecturers, and laughed at old school memories. Saule bought ice cream for everyone from a small kiosk near the fountain. We stayed in the park for almost two hours.

In the evening, we all visited Yerlan's room in the Engineering dormitory — he has a bigger room than the rest of us, with a small kitchen corner. Yerlan cooked rice with chicken — he learned the recipe from his grandmother in Semey and he is actually a very good cook. Aisha prepared a salad. I sliced the bread and arranged everything on the table. We ate together, talked loudly, and played music from a small Bluetooth speaker. After dinner, we watched a film on Yerlan's laptop — a funny Kazakh comedy from 2019. Saule laughed so hard she knocked over her cup of tea!

On Sunday morning, I stayed in bed until nine o'clock and read a novel I had borrowed from the library — a detective story set in Almaty. After breakfast, I helped my roommate Meruert with her Chemistry assignment. She explained her problem and I worked through the calculations with her. It took us about two hours, but she finally understood the topic. She looked so relieved and happy when everything clicked. I was proud of her.

In the afternoon, I returned to the library and worked on my Engineering Design project for three hours. I sketched diagrams, looked up technical terms in English, and typed up my notes. I finished the introduction section completely — something I had planned to do for two weeks! I also emailed my project supervisor to confirm our next meeting. On my way back to the dormitory, I stopped at the small market and bought apples, yoghurt, and some fresh bread.

Sunday evening was quiet and peaceful. I listened to an English podcast about sustainable architecture — a topic I love — and painted a small watercolour picture of the river I had visited the day before. I am not a professional painter, but I enjoyed it so much. I fixed a cup of chamomile tea, placed the painting on my desk to dry, and went to sleep at eleven. As I closed my eyes, I thought: this was a perfect weekend. Work and fun, friends and family, city and campus — everything balanced. I want every weekend to feel like this one.

dialogue.speaker: Yerlan
dialogue.text: Aruzhan! How was your weekend? You look happy!

dialogue.speaker: Aruzhan
dialogue.text: It was amazing! We visited the city park on Saturday — did you enjoy it too?

dialogue.speaker: Yerlan
dialogue.text: Yes! I loved it. And the dinner at my place — did you like the rice?

dialogue.speaker: Aruzhan
dialogue.text: It was delicious! Where did you learn to cook like that?

dialogue.speaker: Yerlan
dialogue.text: My grandmother in Semey taught me. I practised every summer!

dialogue.speaker: Aruzhan
dialogue.text: You should teach us all! What did you do on Sunday?

dialogue.speaker: Yerlan
dialogue.text: I studied all day — I worked on my Economics essay for six hours.

dialogue.speaker: Aruzhan
dialogue.text: Six hours! Did you finish it?

dialogue.speaker: Yerlan
dialogue.text: I finished the first two sections. I wanted to finish it all, but I stopped at midnight.

dialogue.speaker: Aruzhan
dialogue.text: I finished my Engineering introduction! I worked in the library for three hours.

dialogue.speaker: Yerlan
dialogue.text: That's great! And did you call your family?

dialogue.speaker: Aruzhan
dialogue.text: Yes — I talked to my mum and brother for almost an hour on Saturday morning. I missed them!
